items.title: The Brutal Reality of Building Agentic Products Today with Daniel Jeffries - #782
items.summary: AI agents are becoming accessible to everyone, raising the bar for developers building the next generation of agent products. When capable, general-purpose agents are available out of the box, differentiation increasingly comes down to the architectural decisions and specialized experiences that make an agent uniquely valuable. In this episode, Dan Jeffries, creator of Nautilo, joins us to discuss what he's learned building a platform for personal and collaborative AI agents. We explore his approach to persistent memory, coordinating work across people and agents, managing private context, and designing deterministic tools that complement LLM capabilities. Dan also shares his views on multi-agent architectures, computer use, and the tradeoffs between local and cloud models. The conversation offers a practitioner's perspective on where the opportunities lie as AI agents become more capable, more accessible, and more difficult to differentiate. 🗒️ Full show notes: https://twimlai.com/go/782 .

items.title: How Security Leaders Are Responding to Machine Speed Threats - with Sridhar Boddula of MassMutual
items.summary: The cost and skill required to mount a serious cyberattack have collapsed, and most enterprise security programs still test on a quarterly or annual clock. In this episode, Sridhar Boddula, Head of Security Platform Engineering at MassMutual, breaks down why that mismatch is now the central risk for regulated enterprises and what has to change inside a security team to close it. He covers shifting from periodic testing to continuous validation, moving security from a gatekeeping function into the engineering pipeline, and the governance-first first step leaders should take before scaling any new tooling.
